questions.question: What must you keep in your vehicle when transporting chlorine?

options.text: A phone with emergency numbers saved

questions.correctAnswerText: An approved gas mask
questions.explanation: Drivers transporting chlorine in cargo tanks must carry an approved gas mask and an emergency kit in their vehicle.

questions.question: Why could opening trailer doors make a cargo fire worse?

options.text: It lets oxygen into the area.
It changes the temperature of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: It lets oxygen into the area.
questions.explanation: Do not open trailer doors during a cargo fire. Opening them gives the fire more oxygen, which can make it flare up.

questions.question: Hazardous materials warning placards are shaped like a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Diamond
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials warning placards are diamond-shaped.

questions.question: What must shipping papers for hazardous materials include?

options.text: The location of fire departments along the route

questions.correctAnswerText: An emergency response phone number
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials shipping papers must include an emergency response phone number.

questions.question: Your engine runs a pump for compressed gas delivery. After delivery, turn off the engine ____ you unhook the hoses.
questions.correctAnswerText: Before
questions.explanation: If your engine runs a pump for product transfer, turn it off after the transfer is complete but before you unhook the hoses.

questions.question: A person supervising tank loading must:

options.text: Not have to be able to move the vehicle
Not need to know about the materials being loaded
Stay within 25 feet of the tank

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay within 25 feet of the tank
questions.explanation: A qualified person must watch tank loading and unloading. They must stay within 25 feet of the tank, stay alert, watch the tank clearly, know the hazards of the materials, know emergency procedures, and be able to move the tank if needed.

questions.question: If you notice a cargo leak, how can you identify what is leaking?

options.text: By rubbing it on your arm

questions.correctAnswerText: By checking the shipping papers
questions.explanation: If cargo leaks, use the shipping papers, labels, or package locations to identify the materials. Do not touch the leaking materials.

questions.question: Hazardous materials containers must be:

options.text: Secured to prevent movement during transport

questions.correctAnswerText: Secured to prevent movement during transport
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials containers must be secured so they will not fall, slide, or bounce around during transport.

questions.question: An improperly placarded vehicle can be driven:

options.text: If it does not contain radioactive materials

questions.correctAnswerText: Only in an emergency
questions.explanation: Vehicles carrying hazardous materials must be properly placarded. An improperly placarded vehicle may only be driven if necessary to protect life or property in an emergency.

questions.question: At an accident scene, which is not your job as the driver?

options.text: Keeping people away from the scene
Trying to put out a hazardous materials fire
Telling emergency responders about the hazardous materials

questions.correctAnswerText: Trying to put out a hazardous materials fire
questions.explanation: Your job at an accident scene is to keep people away, limit material spread if safe to do so, inform emergency responders of the dangers, and provide shipping papers. Do not try to fight hazardous materials fires yourself unless you have protective equipment and training.

questions.question: Before opening trailer doors during a minor truck fire, what should you do?

options.text: Feel the doors to check if they are hot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Feel the doors to check if they are hot.
questions.explanation: Before opening trailer doors, feel them to check if they are hot. Hot doors mean there may be a cargo fire inside. If the doors are hot, keep them closed.

questions.question: A person loading a tank with hazardous materials must be all of the following, except:

options.text: Aware of the hazards of the materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Within 10 feet of the tank.
questions.explanation: The supervisor must be alert, have a clear view of the tank, be within 25 feet of the tank, know the hazards, know emergency procedures, and be authorized to move the tank.

questions.question: Besides reading the manual, what is the best way to learn about transporting hazardous materials?
questions.correctAnswerText: Take hazardous materials training courses.
questions.explanation: The manual has information needed for the written exam, but training courses teach you how to do the job safely.

questions.question: When a driver stops and leaves the vehicle while transporting hazardous materials, where should shipping papers be placed?

options.text: Leave them on the front seat of the cab.
Place them in a box under the passenger seat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave them on the front seat of the cab.
questions.explanation: Shipping papers must be left on the driver's seat when you leave the vehicle.

questions.question: If hazardous materials cargo is leaking, what should the driver do?

options.text: Drive to find a phone to call emergency personnel.
Drive to a hazardous materials cleanup facility.
Park the vehicle and call emergency personnel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Park the vehicle and call emergency personnel.
questions.explanation: Stop driving as soon as it is safe. Park the vehicle, secure the area, stay with the vehicle, and get help. Continuing to drive spreads contamination over a larger area.

questions.question: If you suspect a leak in radioactive material cargo, what should you do?

options.text: Go to the local fire department.
Pick up any loose pieces of radioactive material.
Continue carrying the cargo if you avoid touching the leak.
Do not operate the vehicle until it has been cleaned.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not operate the vehicle until it has been cleaned.
questions.explanation: Tell your dispatcher or supervisor right away. Do not touch or breathe in the material. Do not use the vehicle until it has been cleaned or checked with a survey meter.

questions.question: Where can hazardous materials shipping papers NOT be kept?

options.text: In a pouch on the driver's door.
In a pouch on the passenger's door.
Within reach of the driver while the seat belt is fastened.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a pouch on the passenger's door.
questions.explanation: Papers must be easy to reach in an emergency. Keep them in a pouch on the driver's door or within reach while your seat belt is on. You can leave them on the driver's seat when you exit the vehicle.

questions.question: What should a driver check about shipping papers?

options.text: The shipping paper matches the markings and labels on packages.
The shipping paper is written in code.
All packages are labeled as poison.

questions.correctAnswerText: The shipping paper matches the markings and labels on packages.
questions.explanation: Compare package labels and markings to the shipping papers. Make sure the shipper used the correct description on the papers and put the right labels on the packages.

questions.question: How should shippers warn others when transporting hazardous materials?

options.text: By posting hazardous materials placards on the truck.
By putting flashing lights on the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: By posting hazardous materials placards on the truck.
questions.explanation: Shippers must display diamond-shaped warning signs, called placards, on vehicles. They must also provide labels, shipping papers, and emergency response information.

questions.question: Class 1, Class 2.1, and Class 3 items should not be placed in a trailer with:
questions.correctAnswerText: A heater.
questions.explanation: Heaters are not allowed when transporting Class 1 (Explosives), Class 2.1 (Flammable Gas), or Class 3 (Flammable Liquids) materials.

questions.question: If hazardous materials cargo is on fire, what should you do?

options.text: Try to put out the fire with a fire extinguisher.
Call emergency personnel and let them handle the fire.
Wait and hope the fire goes out on its own.

questions.correctAnswerText: Call emergency personnel and let them handle the fire.
questions.explanation: Fighting a hazardous materials fire requires special training and equipment. Do not try to fight the fire yourself unless you have the proper training and gear.

questions.question: How long must shippers keep a copy of shipping papers?
questions.correctAnswerText: Two years.
questions.explanation: Shippers must keep a copy or electronic image of hazardous materials shipping papers for at least two years after the carrier accepts the materials. For hazardous waste, the requirement is three years.

questions.question: Hazardous materials regulations protect all of the following, except:
questions.correctAnswerText: Buildings.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials regulations protect the driver, people nearby, and the environment. They are not designed to protect buildings.

questions.question: Where can you find identification numbers for hazardous chemicals?

options.text: In the DOT Emergency Response Guidebook.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the DOT Emergency Response Guidebook.
questions.explanation: The Department of Transportation (DOT) Emergency Response Guidebook lists all hazardous chemicals and their identification numbers.

questions.question: Where can a person attend a placarded vehicle?

options.text: Either awake or asleep inside the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Within 100 feet of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: A person attending a placarded vehicle must be awake inside the vehicle or within 100 feet of it with a clear view. The person may not be in the sleeper berth.

questions.question: What letters appear on shipping papers and packages for reportable quantities?
questions.correctAnswerText: RQ
questions.explanation: When a substance is in a reportable quantity, the shipper must mark the letters "RQ" on the shipping paper and package.

questions.question: What should you do when refueling a vehicle carrying hazardous materials?

options.text: Have someone other than the driver refuel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the engine.
questions.explanation: Always turn off the engine before refueling a vehicle with hazardous materials. Someone must stay at the nozzle while refueling.

questions.question: What is important to know about transporting radioactive materials?

options.text: Radiation spreads around the package and passes through to other packages.
The package should be transported in the cab.
The package should be loaded on its side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Radiation spreads around the package and passes through to other packages.
questions.explanation: Radiation spreads around each radioactive package and can pass through to nearby packages. Rules limit how many packages can be loaded together.

questions.question: Which agency conducts the background check for a HazMat endorsement?
questions.correctAnswerText: Transportation Security Administration
questions.explanation: To get a hazardous materials endorsement, you must pass a background check from the Transportation Security Administration (TSA).

questions.question: What can be a sign that a shipment contains hazardous materials?

options.text: The shipper is a business that typically handles hazardous materials.
Your last shipment was labeled as hazardous.
The road is made of gravel.

questions.correctAnswerText: The shipper is a business that typically handles hazardous materials.
questions.explanation: A clue that a shipment may contain hazardous materials is if the shipper is in a business that works with hazardous materials. Examples include paint dealers, chemical suppliers, scientific suppliers, pest control companies, agricultural suppliers, and explosives dealers.
